steps.text: Maria answers the phone. You have about 20 seconds. Then she decides to stay or go. Good news: you only need **3 letters**.

cards.back: Appointment. A day and time with the agent.
Location. The area and the home they want.
Motivation. Why they want to move, and when.

steps.sub: Get these three on every call.

steps.text: Say **who you are**. Say the call **may be recorded**. Say the **home** they asked about. Then ask for **two minutes**.

items: Hi Maria, this is Ana with Rivera Home Team.

steps.line: Hi Maria, this is Ana with Rivera Home Team. This call may be recorded. You asked about 12 Oak Street.

cards.front: What did you like about that home?

cards.back: L. Where they want to live.

cards.front: Why are you thinking about moving?
When would you like to move?

steps.q: Which question gets a longer answer?
options: What did you like about the home?
steps.why: "What" questions get stories. Yes or no questions do not.

options.text: OK. What is your price, your area and your date?
options.why: Three questions at once is too much. Ask one.

options.text: Tell me more. What does more space look like?
options.why: One easy question. Now she tells you the real need.

options.text: Then buy now. Prices will go up.
options.why: Never push. Never guess about prices.

steps.text: Ask on **every** call. Give **two choices**: a day and a time. Two choices are easy. She just picks one.

options: Daniel can show it Thursday at 5 or Saturday at 11. Which is better?
Let me know if you want to see it.
steps.why: Two real times are easy to answer.

steps.text: Always offer two times. Never ask "When works?"

steps.line: Daniel can show it Thursday at 5 or Saturday at 11. Which is better?

steps.text: She asked about one home. So ask for the tour in the **first minute**. A tour is a visit to the home. Then ask about L and M.

steps.h: Put the two-minute call in order
items: Ask easy questions about the home
Repeat the day, time and place

options.text: I will check with Daniel, our agent, right now. Want to see it tomorrow at 4 or 6?
options.why: Honest. And you asked for the appointment.

options.text: Yes, for sure. It is a great price too.
options.why: Never guess. Never give a price opinion.
Repeat the details first. Then she will not forget.

options.text: Great! I think the seller will take less.
options.why: Never talk about price. That is the agent's job.

options.text: Great! Saturday at 11 at 12 Oak Street with Daniel. Is this your best number?
options.why: You repeat day, time and place. Now it is a real plan.

steps.q: You had a nice 8-minute call. No day, no time. What went wrong?
options: You never asked for the appointment
steps.why: A nice call with no appointment is only a chat.

steps.h: What a great call sounds like
steps.text: You **smile**. People can hear it. You speak **slowly**. The lead talks **more than you**.

steps.q: Maria says, "Sorry? What?" What do you do?
options: Say it again, slower, with easy words
steps.why: Slow and clear wins. Your accent is not a problem.

steps.text: The lead talks more than you.
steps.sub: You ask. You listen. Then you book.

steps.text: Great work! You can now run a two-minute A.L.M. call.

quiz.explain: Appointment, Location, Motivation. Get all three on every call.

quiz.q: Which line is in every opening?
options: How much money do you make?
quiz.explain: Always say the call may be recorded.

quiz.q: How do you ask for the appointment?
options: Wait for the lead to ask
Offer two choices of day and time
quiz.explain: Two choices make it easy to say yes.

quiz.q: "We must move by March." Which letter is this?
quiz.explain: M is Motivation: why they move, and when.

quiz.q: A lead asks about one home. When do you ask for the tour?
options: At the end of a long call
quiz.explain: Ask early. Then ask about L and M.
